scenes.headline: How one small model tells eight voices apart
scenes.sub: Who spoke when, live, sorted by who spoke first.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Sable! A transcript can get every word right and still not say who spoke. Here's how NVIDIA's new diarizer tracks up to eight voices, live.

scenes.text: Output slot one is whoever spoke first, slot two whoever spoke second. A fixed order means nothing to match between chunks.
scenes.say: The trick is an order. Slot one is whoever spoke first, slot two whoever spoke second. With a fixed order, there's nothing to match up between chunks.

left.title: Cluster embeddings
left.say: The classic cascade embeds each segment and clusters the embeddings. One segment gets one speaker, so overlap is lost.

right.title: One network, sorted slots
items: Overlap is two slots on at once
right.say: This model predicts every slot in every frame. Two people talking means two slots on.

scenes.title: From audio to eight speaker slots

steps.say: Audio becomes mel spectrogram frames, one every ten milliseconds.
Eight frames are stacked into one vector, so the encoder works at eighty milliseconds.
A plain thirty-one layer Transformer with rotary positions reads the window.
A small convolution unfolds each vector back to ten milliseconds, and eight sigmoids say who is talking.

items.say: A cache keeps the cleanest seconds of every voice so far, grouped by slot.
Recent frames and the new chunk follow.
The encoder reads it all, so a returning voice lands back in its own slot.
Then the cache is refreshed with frames where one speaker is clearly alone.

scenes.label: parameters, read from the safetensors header
scenes.say: The whole model is about ninety-nine million parameters. I counted them from the file's header.

scenes.title: Average error across 11 datasets
scenes.note: first on VoiceArena at 14.72%; here, a one-point edge
scenes.say: It's first on one English leaderboard by a wide margin. On the broadest public comparison, it edges a commercial service by one point.

scenes.text: Sorting speakers by arrival turns streaming diarization into plain classification: no clustering, no matching.
scenes.say: Sorting speakers by arrival turns streaming diarization into plain classification. No clustering, and no matching.

recap: Slots ordered by who spoke first
A cache of each voice's cleanest seconds
scenes.say: To recap: eight slots, ordered by arrival, and a cache that remembers each voice.
